ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a common-emitter amplifier circuit with voltage-divider bias, and the power supply is +12 V. The base is voltage-divider biased by a 50 kΩ pull-up resistor and a 25 kΩ pull-down resistor, and the input signal is coupled to the base through C1. The collector is connected to +12 V through a 2 kΩ resistor, and the output is coupled to the load on the right through C2. The emitter is connected to a split resistor network: the left and right branches are each composed of 1 kΩ and 1 kΩ in series, and a bypass capacitor CE is connected between the middle nodes. Then reason: When finding the static operating point, C1, C2, and CE are all regarded as open circuits for DC. The emitter DC equivalent resistance is the parallel connection of two branches: each branch is 1 kΩ + 1 kΩ = 2 kΩ, and two 2 kΩ branches in parallel give R_E,dc = 1 kΩ. According to the specified method, treating the base voltage-divider network as an approximately stable voltage divider, the base voltage V_B ≈ 12 × 25/(50 + 25) = 4 V. Given U_BEQ = 0.6 V, the emitter voltage V_E ≈ 4 - 0.6 = 3.4 V. Thus the emitter current I_E ≈ V_E/R_E = 3.4 V / 1 kΩ = 3.4 mA. Since β = 50, under this approximation take I_CQ ≈ I_E, therefore I_CQ ≈ 3.4 mA.

Treat the base divider as stiff: V_B ≈ 12×25/(50+25) = 4 V. Then V_E ≈ 4 - 0.6 = 3.4 V, so I_E ≈ 3.4 V / 1 kΩ = 3.4 mA. The base voltage is therefore set by the 50 kΩ upper and 25 kΩ lower divider, giving the intended fixed bias V_B ≈ 4 V. Translate this base voltage to the emitter node using the given U_BEQ = 0.6 V: V_E ≈ 3.4 V. With β = 50, α ≈ 50/51 ≈ 1, so report I_CQ ≈ I_E = 3.4 mA; a quick check gives V_C ≈ 12 - 3.4 mA·2 kΩ = 5.2 V, above the emitter voltage, so the active-region assumption is consistent.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: The figure is a common-emitter amplifier circuit with voltage-divider bias, and the power supply is +12 V. The base is voltage-divider biased by a 50 kΩ pull-up resistor and a 25 kΩ pull-down resistor, and the input signal is coupled to the base through C1. The collector is connected to +12 V through a 2 kΩ resistor, and the output is coupled to the load on the right through C2. The emitter is connected to a split resistor network: the left and right branches are each composed of 1 kΩ and 1 kΩ in series, and a bypass capacitor CE is connected between the middle nodes.

Then reason: When finding the static operating point, C1, C2, and CE are all regarded as open circuits for DC. The emitter DC equivalent resistance is the parallel connection of two branches: each branch is 1 kΩ + 1 kΩ = 2 kΩ, and two 2 kΩ branches in parallel give R_E,dc = 1 kΩ. According to the specified method, treating the base voltage-divider network as an approximately stable voltage divider, the base voltage V_B ≈ 12 × 25/(50 + 25) = 4 V. Given U_BEQ = 0.6 V, the emitter voltage V_E ≈ 4 - 0.6 = 3.4 V. Thus the emitter current I_E ≈ V_E/R_E = 3.4 V / 1 kΩ = 3.4 mA. Since β = 50, under this approximation take I_CQ ≈ I_E, therefore I_CQ ≈ 3.4 mA.
